answer.evidence: The grade mapping is in radon/metrics.py:150-157, in mi_rank(). It is `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. A score of 9 gives 'C', a score of 19 gives 'B', and anything above 19 gives 'A'. This matches the docstring (A if >19, B if 9<score<=19, C if <=9). The boundary handling is the main thing to review. The bool-arithmetic trick is easy to misread, and the code has no explicit tests at exactly 9 and 19. handoff_refs/C.txt and D.txt contain only generic text with no file-specific priority, so they don't tell me which files matter. I read the instruction to mean the decoded pair is A and B, because the refs name C and D, which are outside it. I gave A (radon/raw.py) and B (radon/complexity.py) 40 minutes in total, as asked. The time goes to checking that they don't hold a competing or duplicate threshold mapping, and to checking how the MI inputs (SLOC and comment counts from raw.py, complexity from the visitors) feed the score. I did not open raw.py or complexity.py, so I have no code evidence from them. The evidence says C is where the answer is, so C is my primary file. A 40-minute split to A and B is probably more than the request needs. 15 minutes on C would be enough to settle the question. D gets 5 minutes.
